title: Global policy institutions are shifting from GDP-only progress toward dashboards that measure well-being, equity, sustainability, resilience, and social cohesion
source_unit: United Nations Secretary-General's High-Level Expert Group on Beyond GDP, Counting What Counts: A Compass of Progress for People and Planet
geography: Global framework for country-owned and universally applicable progress indicators, with UNCTAD implementation and pilot context

denominator.unit: headline and dashboard indicators proposed by the UN High-Level Expert Group on Beyond GDP

dashboard_pillars.unit: foundational principles; current well-being; equity and inclusion; sustainability and resilience

current_wellbeing_domains.value: material conditions and work, health, education, security, subjective well-being

equity_and_inclusion_domains.value: wealth inequality, income inequality, poverty, work inclusion, regional inequalities, overlapping deprivations, social cohesion

sustainability_and_resilience_domains.value: produced, human, social, institutional, and natural capital plus environmental quality

observations.method: UN High-Level Expert Group synthesis of existing statistical systems, SDG indicators, well-being measurement, distributional analysis, sustainability, resilience, and foundational principles.
observations.uncertainty: The dashboard is a proposed framework rather than a completed global time series; indicator availability, comparability, country ownership, and political adoption remain implementation questions.
observations.subgroup: Governments, statistical offices, multilateral institutions, civil society, media, communities, and populations whose well-being is not captured by aggregate economic output.
observations.counterinterpretation: GDP remains useful for measuring economic activity; a broader dashboard should complement rather than replace output measures, and multiple indicators can create trade-offs or political contestation.

denominator.unit: global policy-measurement framework and decision-use case

gdp_blind_spot.value: economic growth can coexist with deteriorating safety, environmental quality, inequality, health, education, or peace

foundational_principles.value: human rights, peace, and respect for the planet
foundational_principles.unit: principles proposed as foundations for progress measurement

policy_use.value: country-owned dashboards embedded in policy-making and decision-making

observations.method: UN expert-group framework connecting measurement choices to policy priorities, public communication, accountability, and institutional decision-making.
observations.uncertainty: Changing indicators does not automatically change budgets, distribution, political incentives, or lived outcomes; implementation can be selective, symbolic, or contested.
observations.subgroup: People affected by poverty, inequality, environmental degradation, insecurity, weak public services, regional disparities, and undercounted non-market contributions.
observations.counterinterpretation: A dashboard can improve visibility without resolving value conflicts; democratic deliberation and policy capacity are still required to decide which trade-offs are acceptable.

observations.period: 2026; international statistical implementation and cross-border spillovers

denominator.unit: UN and country implementation pathway for beyond-GDP indicators

country_ownership.unit: country-owned and universally applicable indicator approach

cross_border_spillovers.unit: recognition that well-being in one country can be influenced by decisions and activities in other countries

implementation_role.value: UNCTAD pilots proposed indicators and supports country-level adoption through statistical and policy expertise

observations.method: UN and UNCTAD implementation description covering country pilots, official statistics, the Global Alliance of Beyond GDP, and multilateral reporting.
observations.uncertainty: Pilots and proposed indicators do not establish harmonized adoption, data quality, financing, or sustained use in national decisions; cross-border effects are difficult to attribute to individual countries.
observations.subgroup: National statistical systems, international organizations, development-finance institutions, policymakers, civil society, media, and communities affected by transnational economic and environmental spillovers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Country ownership can improve relevance and legitimacy but may reduce comparability; universal indicators can improve comparability but risk missing culturally specific values and local priorities.

related_sources.claim: UN Beyond GDP documents and full-report landing page.
UN launch summary and policy rationale for the dashboard.

boundary: This record adds a measurement-to-policy-legitimacy route: how institutions define progress, make inequality and environmental conditions visible, and potentially change decision criteria. It is not a well-being survey, respondent-level outcome, causal policy evaluation, or claim that dashboard adoption has already changed public behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN HLEG report, UN launch release, Beyond GDP documents page, and UNCTAD implementation page were retrieved; dashboard pillars, domains, indicator count, foundational principles, country ownership, spillovers, and pilot claims were cross-checked.
